notes: Customer snapshot: mid-market B2B SaaS (workflow automation) with a productized smart assistant that surfaces documents and automates replies.
Why Redwood: likes unified runtime + transparent perf. Hates opaque token pricing models. Wants predictable per-qps pricing for core search flows.
POC highlights: hosted API easy to integrate; quick iteration with SDKs. P95 latency acceptable in sandbox but production peaks caused inconsistent tail latency.
Primary move to Dedicated: need predictable throughput for synchronous support-agent flows (SLAs to their customers), VPC peering, and KMS-managed keys for logs and KV cache encryption.
Performance targets requested by product: p95 generation latency <= 100ms for 256-token window on dedicated pool; sustained throughput 120–180 QPS for search/rerank route.
Quality: prefer open-model variants compatible with Redwood model catalog — leaning toward Llama-3 family quantized; fallbacks to smaller variants during maintenance windows.
Security/legal asks: standard MSA redlines around liability cap, indemnity carveouts, data residency (US-region only), right-to-audit, subprocessors list; DPA with 90-day delete/retention options.
SAML/SSO: Product team wants SSO for admin console, SCIM for provisioning (timeline: 4–6 weeks). SE flagged SSO as must-have before go-live.
KMS: Asked for compatibility checklist for AWS KMS and key rotation policy. Also asked if HSM-backed keys are available for Dedicated (customer may require for enterprise customers).
Procurement note: Finance requested a 12-month commitment quote with committed capacity discount tiers and clear escalation path for SLA incidents.
"Integration was straightforward — SDKs removed friction. Now need guaranteed latency for live support flows." — VP Product
"Legal: we will not accept unlimited liability; propose 2x ARR cap and negotiated carveouts." — Procurement lead
Operational concerns: onboarding windows, expected IP ranges for VPC peering, logging retention and live incident runbook access.
Evals done: load test on hosted instance (50–200 concurrent simulated users) — tail latencies at peak suggest Dedicated with dedicated GPU pool would smooth results.
Recommended Redwood asks: provide Dedicated onboarding checklist, SOC2 support bundle, sample SLA with latency SLOs, clear quantization/model variant docs and KMS/HSM integration guide.
Open: final countersignature, confirm timeline for Dedicated provisioning (expected 2–3 weeks after countersign), confirm exact ARR and invoicing term.
